माना कुंडली में \(N\) फेरे तथा क्षेत्रफल \(A\) है। चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(\vec{B}\) और क्षेत्रफल सदिश के बीच कोण \(\theta = \omega t\) होने पर संबद्ध फ्लक्स \(\Phi_B = B A \cos(\omega t)\) होता है। फैराडे के नियम से प्रेरित वि.वा.बल \(\varepsilon = -N\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t} = N B A \omega \sin(\omega t)\) होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
जब कुंडली का तल चुंबकीय क्षेत्र के समानांतर होता है, तो क्षेत्रफल सदिश और चुंबकीय क्षेत्र के बीच कोण \(\theta = 90^\circ\) होता है। इस स्थिति में \(\sin(\omega t) = 1\) होता है और वि.वा.बल का परिमाण अधिकतम \(|\varepsilon|_{\text{max}} = N B A \omega\) होता है। इसलिए कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
जब फ्लक्स अधिकतम होता है (\(\theta = 0^\circ\)), तब \(\cos(\omega t) = 1\) होता है, परंतु इस क्षण \(\sin(\omega t) = 0\) होने के कारण प्रेरित वि.वा.बल शून्य होता है। फ्लक्स के चरम मान पर उसका अवकलन (समय दर) शून्य होता है। इसलिए कथन II गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I सही है लेकिन कथन II गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETICINDUCTION_MCQ_Q08 - Nature of induced electric field and mechanical to electrical power balance

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The electric field produced by a time-varying magnetic field is a conservative field, and its line integral around any closed loop is always identically zero.

Statement II: In a motional emf circuit where a rod of length \(l\) and resistance \(R\) moves at steady speed \(v\) across frictionless rails in a uniform magnetic field \(B\), the mechanical power supplied by an external agent to maintain motion exactly equals the rate of Joule heat dissipation \(P = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: समय के साथ बदलते चुंबकीय क्षेत्र द्वारा उत्पन्न विद्युत क्षेत्र एक संरक्षी क्षेत्र होता है, तथा किसी बंद लूप के परितः इसका रेखा समाकलन सदैव शून्य होता है।

कथन II: गतिक वि.वा.बल परिपथ में जहाँ \(l\) लंबाई और \(R\) प्रतिरोध की एक छड़ एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(B\) में घर्षण रहित पटरियों पर स्थिर चाल \(v\) से गति करती है, गति बनाए रखने के लिए बाह्य कारक द्वारा दी गई यांत्रिक शक्ति जूल ऊष्मा क्षय की दर \(P = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}\) के ठीक बराबर होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
By Faraday's law in integral form, a time-varying magnetic flux produces an electric field whose circulation around a closed contour is non-zero: \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\). In motional emf, conservation of energy demands that external mechanical power converts into thermal power via Joule heating.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
For an electrostatic field produced by static charges, \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = 0\), which defines a conservative field. However, the electric field induced by a changing magnetic field has closed field lines, and its closed loop line integral equals the induced emf \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t} \neq 0\). Because the loop integral is non-zero, this induced electric field is non-conservative in nature. Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
The induced emf in the moving rod is \(\varepsilon = B l v\), resulting in an induced current \(I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R} = \frac{B l v}{R}\). The magnetic retarding force on the rod is \(F_m = I l B = \frac{B^2 l^2 v}{R}\). To keep the rod moving at constant speed \(v\), the external pulling force must balance this force: \(F_{\text{ext}} = F_m\). The mechanical power delivered is \(P_{\text{mech}} = F_{\text{ext}} v = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}\). The rate of thermal energy dissipated as Joule heat is \(P_{\text{Joule}} = I^2 R = \left(\frac{B l v}{R}\right)^2 R = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}\). Thus, mechanical power precisely equals the rate of thermal dissipation, in accordance with the law of conservation of energy. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Final Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
फैराडे के नियम के समाकल रूप के अनुसार, समय-परिवर्ती चुंबकीय फ्लक्स एक विद्युत क्षेत्र उत्पन्न करता है जिसका रेखा समाकलन \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\) होता है। गतिक वि.वा.बल में ऊर्जा संरक्षण के अनुसार यांत्रिक शक्ति पूर्णतः जूल ऊष्मा में परिवर्तित होती है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
स्थिरवैद्युत क्षेत्र संरक्षी होता है तथा उसका रेखा समाकलन शून्य होता है। परंतु बदलते चुंबकीय क्षेत्र द्वारा उत्पन्न प्रेरित विद्युत क्षेत्र की रेखाएं बंद वक्र बनाती हैं और इसका बंद लूप समाकलन \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} \neq 0\) होता है। शून्य न होने के कारण यह क्षेत्र असंरक्षी (non-conservative) होता है। इसलिए कथन I गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
चालक छड़ में उत्पन्न धारा \(I = \frac{B l v}{R}\) तथा चुंबकीय विरोधी बल \(F = \frac{B^2 l^2 v}{R}\) होता है। नियत चाल \(v\) से चलाने के लिए बाह्य शक्ति \(P_{\text{mech}} = F v = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}\) आवश्यक है। परिपथ में उत्पन्न जूल ऊष्मा की दर \(P = I^2 R = \frac{B^2 l^2 v^2}{R}\) होती है, जो यांत्रिक शक्ति के ठीक बराबर है। इसलिए कथन II सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I गलत है लेकिन कथन II सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETICINDUCTION_MCQ_Q01 - Magnetic flux definition and Faraday law dependence

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Magnetic flux through a planar surface placed in a uniform magnetic field is a scalar quantity given by the scalar product of the magnetic field vector and the area vector.

Statement II: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber (\(\text{Wb}\)), which is equivalent to tesla meter squared (\(\text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2\)) and volt-second (\(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\)).

Statement III: According to Faraday's law of induction, the magnitude of the induced electromotive force in a coil is directly proportional to the total magnitude of magnetic flux linked with the coil, regardless of its time rate of change.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र में रखे किसी समतलीय पृष्ठ से संबद्ध चुंबकीय फ्लक्स एक अदिश राशि है, जो चुंबकीय क्षेत्र सदिश और क्षेत्रफल सदिश के अदिश गुणनफल द्वारा प्राप्त होती है।

कथन II: चुंबकीय फ्लक्स का SI मात्रक वेबर (\(\text{Wb}\)) है, जो टेस्ला मीटर वर्ग (\(\text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2\)) तथा वोल्ट-सेकंड (\(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\)) के समतुल्य है।

कथन III: फैराडे के प्रेरण के नियमानुसार, किसी कुंडली में प्रेरित विद्युत वाहक बल का परिमाण कुंडली से संबद्ध कुल चुंबकीय फ्लक्स के परिमाण के सीधे समानुपाती होता है, चाहे इसके समय के साथ परिवर्तन की दर कुछ भी हो।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Magnetic flux through a surface of area \(\vec{A}\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\) is defined as \(\Phi_B = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A} = B A \cos \theta\). Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction states that the induced electromotive force in a circuit is governed by the time rate of change of magnetic flux: \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
The definition \(\Phi_B = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A}\) is the scalar (dot) product of two vectors, which yields a scalar quantity. Thus, magnetic flux is a scalar quantity. Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
The SI unit of magnetic field is tesla (\(\text{T}\)) and of area is \(\text{m}^2\), giving the weber (\(\text{Wb} = \text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2\)). Furthermore, from \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\), we have \([\Phi_B] = [\varepsilon][t] = \text{V}\cdot\text{s}\). Thus, \(1\text{ Wb} = 1\text{ T}\cdot\text{m}^2 = 1\text{ V}\cdot\text{s}\). Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
Faraday's law explicitly asserts that the induced electromotive force depends on the time rate of change of flux, \(|\varepsilon| = \left|\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\right|\), and not on the absolute magnitude of the flux linked with the circuit. A large, constant magnetic flux yields zero induced emf. Therefore, Statement III is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement II only are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(\vec{B}\) में स्थित क्षेत्रफल \(\vec{A}\) वाले पृष्ठ से संबद्ध चुंबकीय फ्लक्स \(\Phi_B = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A} = B A \cos \theta\) द्वारा परिभाषित होता है। फैराडे के प्रेरण नियमानुसार प्रेरित वि.वा.बल फ्लक्स में समय के साथ परिवर्तन की दर \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\) पर निर्भर करता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
फ्लक्स \(\Phi_B = \vec{B} \cdot \vec{A}\) दो सदिशों का अदिश (डॉट) गुणनफल है, जो सदैव एक अदिश राशि होती है। अतः चुंबकीय फ्लक्स एक अदिश राशि है। इसलिए कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
चुंबकीय क्षेत्र का मात्रक टेस्ला (\(\text{T}\)) और क्षेत्रफल का मात्रक \(\text{m}^2\) होने से फ्लक्स का SI मात्रक वेबर (\(\text{Wb} = \text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2\)) होता है। साथ ही \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\) से इसका मात्रक वोल्ट-सेकंड (\(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\)) भी होता है। इसलिए कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
फैराडे के नियम के अनुसार प्रेरित वि.वा.बल चुंबकीय फ्लक्स के समय के साथ परिवर्तन की दर \(|\varepsilon| = \left|\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\right|\) पर निर्भर करता है, न कि फ्लक्स के कुल परिमाण पर। यदि अत्यधिक फ्लक्स भी स्थिर रहे, तो प्रेरित वि.वा.बल शून्य होता है। इसलिए कथन III गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन II सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETICINDUCTION_MCQ_Q02 - Lenz law polarity conservation of energy and magnet motion

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: When a bar magnet is dropped vertically along the axis of a stationary horizontal copper ring, the downward acceleration of the falling magnet is always greater than the acceleration due to gravity \(g\).

Statement II: Lenz's law dictates the polarity of an induced electromotive force and is a direct consequence of the principle of conservation of energy.

Statement III: When the North pole of a bar magnet is pulled away from a closed conducting coil, the current induced in the coil flows in a direction such that the facing side behaves as a magnetic South pole.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब एक दंड चुंबक को एक स्थिर क्षैतिज तांबे के वलय की अक्ष के अनुदिश ऊर्ध्वाधर नीचे गिराया जाता है, तो गिरते हुए चुंबक का नीचे की ओर त्वरण सदैव गुरुत्वीय त्वरण \(g\) से अधिक होता है।

कथन II: लेंज का नियम प्रेरित विद्युत वाहक बल की ध्रुवता निर्धारित करता है और यह ऊर्जा संरक्षण के सिद्धांत का एक प्रत्यक्ष परिणाम है।

कथन III: जब किसी दंड चुंबक के उत्तरी ध्रुव को एक बंद चालक कुंडली से दूर खींचा जाता है, तो कुंडली में प्रेरित धारा इस प्रकार बहती है कि चुंबक के सम्मुख फलक एक चुंबकीय दक्षिणी ध्रुव की भांति व्यवहार करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Lenz's law states that the polarity of induced emf is such that it tends to produce an induced current that opposes the change in magnetic flux producing it. This opposition ensures that mechanical work must be done against electromagnetic forces to sustain the process, thereby conserving energy.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
As the magnet falls toward the ring, the downward magnetic flux through the ring increases. By Lenz's law, the induced current in the ring produces an opposing magnetic field with a like pole facing the approaching magnet, creating an upward repulsive force. After the magnet passes through and falls away, an attractive upward force retards its motion. Consequently, the net downward acceleration is always less than \(g\) (i.e., \(a < g\)), never greater than \(g\). Therefore, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
If the induced current aided rather than opposed the change in flux, a gentle push would cause perpetual acceleration without energy expenditure, violating conservation of energy. The mechanical energy spent in overcoming the opposition is dissipated as Joule heating. Thus, Lenz's law is a direct consequence of the conservation of energy. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
When the North pole is withdrawn, the magnetic flux through the coil decreases. To oppose this decrease, the induced current must attract the receding North pole. An attractive force requires an unlike magnetic pole, so the facing side of the coil acts as a South pole. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Final Answer: Statement II and Statement III only are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
लेंज के नियमानुसार प्रेरित वि.वा.बल की ध्रुवता इस प्रकार होती है कि वह उस चुंबकीय फ्लक्स परिवर्तन का विरोध करती है जिससे वह उत्पन्न हुआ है। यह विरोध यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि परिपथ में ऊर्जा संरक्षण का नियम पूर्णतः लागू रहे।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
जब चुंबक वलय की ओर गिरता है, तो फ्लक्स में वृद्धि का विरोध करने के लिए वलय में प्रेरित धारा चुंबक पर ऊपर की ओर प्रतिकर्षण बल लगाती है। वलय से पार निकलने पर यह आकर्षण बल द्वारा चुंबक को ऊपर खींचती है। अतः दोनों स्थितियों में नीचे की ओर कुल त्वरण गुरुत्वीय त्वरण से कम (\(a < g\)) होता है, अधिक नहीं। इसलिए कथन I गलत है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
यदि प्रेरित धारा फ्लक्स परिवर्तन का सहयोग करती, तो बिना ऊर्जा दिए निरंतर त्वरण प्राप्त होता जो ऊर्जा संरक्षण के विपरीत होता। चुंबक को गति कराने में किया गया यांत्रिक कार्य ही जूल ऊष्मा के रूप में परिवर्तित होता है। अतः लेंज का नियम ऊर्जा संरक्षण का प्रत्यक्ष परिणाम है। इसलिए कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
जब उत्तरी ध्रुव को कुंडली से दूर ले जाया जाता है, तो फ्लक्स घटने लगता है। इस कमी का विरोध करने के लिए कुंडली का सम्मुख सिरा दूर जाते उत्तरी ध्रुव को आकर्षित करने हेतु दक्षिणी ध्रुव बनाता है। इसलिए कथन III सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल कथन II और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETICINDUCTION_MCQ_Q03 - Motional emf across moving rod and solenoid self inductance dependence

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: When a straight metallic rod of length \(l\) moves at constant speed \(v\) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field \(B\), the magnitude of the motional electromotive force induced between its ends is \(B l v\).

Statement II: The self-inductance of a long air-core solenoid of fixed length \(l\) and fixed cross-sectional area \(A\) is inversely proportional to the square of its total number of turns \(N\).

Statement III: Self-inductance of a coil is analogous to mass in mechanics because it represents electrical inertia that opposes any change in the current flowing through it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब \(l\) लंबाई की एक सीधी धात्विक छड़ एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(B\) के लंबवत नियत चाल \(v\) से गति करती है, तो उसके सिरों के बीच प्रेरित गतिक विद्युत वाहक बल का परिमाण \(B l v\) होता है।

कथन II: नियत लंबाई \(l\) तथा नियत अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल \(A\) वाली एक लंबी वायु-क्रोड परिनालिका का स्व-प्रेरकत्व उसके कुल फेरों की संख्या \(N\) के वर्ग के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है।

कथन III: किसी कुंडली का स्व-प्रेरकत्व यांत्रिकी में द्रव्यमान के समरूप होता है क्योंकि यह विद्युत जड़त्व को दर्शाता है जो इसमें प्रवाहित धारा के किसी भी परिवर्तन का विरोध करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
Motional emf arises from the Lorentz force acting on mobile conduction charges inside a moving conductor: \(\varepsilon = \int (\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l}\). Self-inductance \(L\) connects flux linkage to current: \(N\Phi_B = L I\), and stored magnetic energy \(U = \frac{1}{2} L I^2\) mirrors mechanical kinetic energy \(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
For a straight rod moving perpendicular to both its length and the magnetic field \(B\), every charge experiences a magnetic Lorentz force \(q v B\). The work done per unit charge in moving from one end to the other is \(\varepsilon = \frac{W}{q} = B l v\). Thus, the induced motional emf is indeed \(B l v\). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
For a solenoid with \(N\) turns, length \(l\), and area \(A\), the magnetic field inside is \(B = \mu_0 (N/l) I\). The total flux linkage is \(N\Phi_B = N(BA) = N \left(\mu_0 \frac{N}{l} I\right) A = \frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l} I\). Hence, self-inductance is \(L = \frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}\). This shows that \(L\) is directly proportional to \(N^2\), not inversely proportional. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
The self-induced emf \(\varepsilon = -L \frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\) always opposes any increase or decrease in current, acting as electrical inertia. In comparing magnetic energy \(\frac{1}{2} L I^2\) with kinetic energy \(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\), self-inductance \(L\) plays the role of mass \(m\). Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Final Answer: Statement I and Statement III only are correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
गतिक वि.वा.बल गतिमान चालक के मुक्त आवेशों पर लगने वाले लॉरेंट्ज़ बल से उत्पन्न होता है: \(\varepsilon = B l v\)। स्व-प्रेरकत्व \(L\) कुल फ्लक्स संबद्धता \(N\Phi_B = L I\) द्वारा निर्धारित होता है तथा संचित चुंबकीय ऊर्जा \(U = \frac{1}{2} L I^2\) यांत्रिक गतिज ऊर्जा के अनुरूप होती है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
चुंबकीय क्षेत्र \(B\) के लंबवत \(v\) चाल से गतिमान \(l\) लंबाई की छड़ में प्रति इकाई आवेश पर किया गया कार्य \(\varepsilon = B l v\) होता है। अतः प्रेरित गतिक वि.वा.बल \(B l v\) है। इसलिए कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
लंबाई \(l\) तथा क्षेत्रफल \(A\) की परिनालिका का स्व-प्रेरकत्व \(L = \frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}\) होता है। अतः स्व-प्रेरकत्व फेरों की संख्या के वर्ग के सीधे समानुपाती (\(L \propto N^2\)) होता है, व्युत्क्रमानुपाती नहीं। इसलिए कथन II गलत है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
प्रेरकत्व द्वारा उत्पन्न विरोधी वि.वा.बल \(\varepsilon = -L \frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\) धारा परिवर्तन का विरोध करता है। ऊर्जा समीकरण \(\frac{1}{2} L I^2\) की तुलना \(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\) से करने पर \(L\) द्रव्यमान \(m\) की भांति विद्युत जड़त्व का कार्य करता है। इसलिए कथन III सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: केवल कथन I और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETICINDUCTION_MCQ_Q04 - AC generator armature orientation nonconservative electric field and reciprocity

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In an alternating current (AC) generator, the instantaneous electromotive force induced in the rotating armature coil is zero at the instant when the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field lines.

Statement II: The electric field induced along a closed stationary loop by a time-varying magnetic field is non-conservative because the line integral of the electric field around the closed loop is non-zero.

Statement III: For any two co-axial solenoids, the mutual inductance of the first solenoid with respect to the second is identically equal to the mutual inductance of the second solenoid with respect to the first (\(M_{12} = M_{21}\)).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा (AC) जनरेटर में, घूर्णन करती आर्मेचर कुंडली में तात्क्षणिक प्रेरित विद्युत वाहक बल उस क्षण शून्य होता है जब कुंडली का तल चुंबकीय क्षेत्र रेखाओं के लंबवत होता है।

कथन II: समय के साथ बदलते चुंबकीय क्षेत्र द्वारा किसी स्थिर बंद लूप के अनुदिश प्रेरित विद्युत क्षेत्र असंरक्षी होता है क्योंकि बंद लूप के परितः विद्युत क्षेत्र का रेखा समाकलन अशून्य होता है।

कथन III: किन्हीं दो समाक्षीय परिनालिकाओं के लिए, दूसरी परिनालिका के सापेक्ष पहली परिनालिका का अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व, पहली परिनालिका के सापेक्ष दूसरी परिनालिका के अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व के सर्वसम बराबर होता है (\(M_{12} = M_{21}\))।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle:
In an AC generator, instantaneous emf is given by \(\varepsilon = NBA\omega \sin(\omega t)\) where \(\omega t\) is the angle between the normal to the coil and the magnetic field. A time-varying magnetic field produces an induced electric field with non-zero curl, \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\). The mutual inductance between two circuits satisfies the reciprocity theorem \(M_{12} = M_{21}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I:
When the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the area vector (normal to the plane) is parallel to the field, so \(\theta = \omega t = 0^\circ\). At this position, the magnetic flux is at its maximum value \(\Phi_B = B A\), but its instantaneous rate of change is zero because \(\sin(0^\circ) = 0\). Hence, the induced emf is \(\varepsilon = NBA\omega \sin(0^\circ) = 0\). Therefore, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II:
A conservative electric field requires \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = 0\) along every closed path. For an electric field induced by a changing magnetic field, Faraday's law in integral form yields \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t} \neq 0\). Because this closed path integral is non-zero, work done along a closed loop is non-zero, demonstrating that the induced electric field is non-conservative. Therefore, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III:
As established in NCERT Section 6.7.1, whether calculating the flux linkage in coil 1 due to current in coil 2 (\(M_{12} = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 \pi r_1^2 l\)) or in coil 2 due to current in coil 1 (\(M_{21} = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 \pi r_1^2 l\)), the equality \(M_{12} = M_{21} = M\) strictly holds true. This is the reciprocity theorem of mutual induction. Therefore, Statement III is correct.

Final Answer: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत:
प्रत्यावर्ती धारा जनरेटर में तात्क्षणिक वि.वा.बल \(\varepsilon = NBA\omega \sin(\omega t)\) होता है। फैराडे के नियम के अनुसार परिवर्ती चुंबकीय क्षेत्र द्वारा उत्पन्न प्रेरित विद्युत क्षेत्र का रेखा समाकलन \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t}\) होता है। अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व में व्युत्क्रमणीयता प्रमेय से \(M_{12} = M_{21}\) मान्य होता है।

चरण 2: कथन I का मूल्यांकन:
जब कुंडली का तल चुंबकीय क्षेत्र के लंबवत होता है, तो क्षेत्रफल सदिश क्षेत्र के समानांतर (\(\theta = 0^\circ\)) होता है। इस क्षण फ्लक्स अधिकतम होता है, परंतु उसके परिवर्तन की दर शून्य (\(\sin 0^\circ = 0\)) होती है, जिससे प्रेरित वि.वा.बल \(\varepsilon = 0\) होता है। इसलिए कथन I सही है।

चरण 3: कथन II का मूल्यांकन:
संरक्षी क्षेत्र के लिए किसी बंद लूप के परितः रेखा समाकलन शून्य होना अनिवार्य है। प्रेरित विद्युत क्षेत्र के लिए \(\oint \vec{E} \cdot \mathrm{d}\vec{l} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_B}{\mathrm{d}t} \neq 0\) होता है, जो यह सिद्ध करता है कि प्रेरित विद्युत क्षेत्र असंरक्षी (non-conservative) है। इसलिए कथन II सही है।

चरण 4: कथन III का मूल्यांकन:
दो समाक्षीय परिनालिकाओं के लिए अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व \(M_{12} = M_{21} = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 \pi r_1^2 l\) दोनों दिशाओं में समान प्राप्त होता है। यह व्युत्क्रमणीयता संबंध सार्वभौमिक रूप से सत्य है। इसलिए कथन III सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: कथन I, कथन II और कथन III तीनों सही हैं।

answer.text: Statement I and Statement II only are correct
Statement II and Statement III only are correct
Statement I and Statement III only are correct
Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are all correct

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_MATCHING_Q01 - Physical quantities and their SI units

questiontext.text:
Match the physical quantities related to electromagnetic induction in List I with their corresponding SI units or dimensional representations in List II:

List I (Physical Quantity) List II (SI Unit / Dimension)
(A) Magnetic flux (\(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}\)) (I) \(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\cdot\text{A}^{-1}\) or henry (\(\text{H}\))
(B) Induced electromotive force (\(\varepsilon\)) (II) \(\text{J}\cdot\text{m}^{-3}\) or \([\mathrm{M}\,\mathrm{L}^{-1}\,\mathrm{T}^{-2}]\)
(C) Self-inductance (\(L\)) (III) \(\text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2\) or weber (\(\text{Wb}\))
(D) Magnetic energy density (\(u_{\mathrm{B}}\)) (IV) \(\text{J}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or volt (\(\text{V}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The quantities under consideration are magnetic flux, induced electromotive force, self-inductance, and magnetic energy density.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Magnetic flux is defined by \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = \int \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathrm{d}\mathbf{A}\). The product of magnetic field in tesla (\(\text{T}\)) and area in square meters (\(\text{m}^2\)) gives the unit weber (\(\text{Wb}\)), which is equivalent to \(\text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2\) or \(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\).
2. Induced electromotive force represents electric potential difference, defined as work done per unit electric charge, \(\varepsilon = \frac{W}{q}\). The SI unit is joule per coulomb (\(\text{J}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\)), universally known as volt (\(\text{V}\)).
3. Self-inductance is defined from the induced emf relation \(\varepsilon = -L\,\frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\), giving \(L = \frac{\varepsilon}{\mathrm{d}I/\mathrm{d}t}\). The corresponding SI unit is volt-second per ampere (\(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\cdot\text{A}^{-1}\)), termed henry (\(\text{H}\)).
4. Magnetic energy density is magnetic energy stored per unit volume, \(u_{\mathrm{B}} = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0} = \frac{U}{V}\). The SI unit is joule per cubic meter (\(\text{J}\cdot\text{m}^{-3}\)), corresponding to the dimensions of pressure or energy per volume, \([\mathrm{M}\,\mathrm{L}^{-1}\,\mathrm{T}^{-2}]\).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working and Evaluation
Matching each physical quantity with its unique SI unit or dimensional representation:
- Magnetic flux pairs with \(\text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2\) or weber (\(\text{Wb}\)).
- Induced electromotive force pairs with \(\text{J}\cdot\text{C}^{-1}\) or volt (\(\text{V}\)).
- Self-inductance pairs with \(\text{V}\cdot\text{s}\cdot\text{A}^{-1}\) or henry (\(\text{H}\)).
- Magnetic energy density pairs with \(\text{J}\cdot\text{m}^{-3}\) or \([\mathrm{M}\,\mathrm{L}^{-1}\,\mathrm{T}^{-2}]\).

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Dimensional consistency verifies each assignment. The correct matching sequence associates magnetic flux with weber, induced emf with volt, self-inductance with henry, and magnetic energy density with joules per cubic meter.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_MATCHING_Q02 - Electromagnetic principles and governing mathematical formulations

questiontext.text:
Match the physical laws and phenomena of electromagnetic induction in List I with their fundamental statements or governing mathematical expressions in List II:

List I (Law / Phenomenon) List II (Statement / Governing Expression)
(A) Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction (I) Direct manifestation of the law of conservation of energy
(B) Lenz's law (II) \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}t}\)
(C) Motional emf for a straight rod translating perpendicularly in uniform \(\mathbf{B}\) (III) \(\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2}B\omega R^2\)
(D) Induced emf in a conducting rod of length \(R\) rotating about one end in uniform \(\mathbf{B}\) (IV) \(\varepsilon = B l v\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The phenomena and principles are Faraday's law, Lenz's law, motional emf of a translating straight conductor, and induced emf of a rotating conducting rod.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. Faraday's law states that the magnitude of the induced electromotive force in a circuit is equal to the time rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit: \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}t}\).
2. Lenz's law gives the polarity of the induced emf such that it tends to produce a current which opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it. It is a direct consequence of the law of conservation of energy; mechanical work done against the opposing electromagnetic force is converted into electrical energy.
3. A straight conducting rod of length \(l\) moving with speed \(v\) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field \(B\) sweeps an area at the rate \(\frac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}t} = l v\), inducing a motional emf given by \(\varepsilon = B l v\).
4. A conducting rod of length \(R\) rotating with constant angular velocity \(\omega\) in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field \(B\) about one pivoted end has an average linear velocity of \(\frac{0 + \omega R}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\omega R\). The induced emf between the pivot and the rim is \(\varepsilon = B \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}t} = B \left(\frac{1}{2}R^2 \omega\right) = \frac{1}{2}B\omega R^2\).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working and Evaluation
Correlating each item:
- Faraday's law of induction corresponds to \(\varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}t}\).
- Lenz's law corresponds to the direct manifestation of the law of conservation of energy.
- Motional emf in a straight translating rod corresponds to \(\varepsilon = B l v\).
- Induced emf in a rotating conducting rod corresponds to \(\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2}B\omega R^2\).

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Each relationship is verified by standard electromagnetic theory and conservation laws. The correct match links Faraday's law with the flux derivative formula, Lenz's law with conservation of energy, the translating rod with \(B l v\), and the rotating rod with \(\frac{1}{2}B\omega R^2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_MATCHING_Q03 - Inductance and magnetic energy relations in solenoids and circuits

questiontext.text:
Match the electromagnetic quantities and concepts in List I with their corresponding mathematical expressions in List II (symbols have their usual meanings):

List I (Quantity / Concept) List II (Mathematical Expression)
(A) Self-inductance of a long air-core solenoid of area \(A\) and length \(l\) (I) \(\varepsilon = -L\,\frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\)
(B) Mutual inductance of two concentric coaxial long solenoids of radii \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) (\(r_1 < r_2\)) (II) \(U = \frac{1}{2}L I^2\)
(C) Magnetic potential energy stored in an inductor carrying steady current \(I\) (III) \(L = \mu_0 n^2 A l\)
(D) Back electromotive force induced in an inductor due to time-varying current (IV) \(M = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 \pi r_1^2 l\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The quantities analyzed are the self-inductance of a solenoid, mutual inductance of concentric solenoids, magnetic energy stored in an inductor, and self-induced back electromotive force.

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. For a long solenoid of cross-sectional area \(A\), length \(l\), and number of turns per unit length \(n\), the magnetic field is \(B = \mu_0 n I\). The total magnetic flux linkage is \(N\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = (n l)(B A) = \mu_0 n^2 A l I\). By definition \(N\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = L I\), giving self-inductance \(L = \mu_0 n^2 A l\).
2. For two coaxial solenoids where solenoid 1 has radius \(r_1\) and solenoid 2 has radius \(r_2\) (\(r_1 < r_2\)), the magnetic field produced by current in the outer solenoid is confined over area \(\pi r_1^2\) for flux linkage through the inner solenoid. The mutual inductance per unit length is \(M = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 \pi r_1^2 l\).
3. The rate of work done to establish current against back emf is \(\frac{\mathrm{d}W}{\mathrm{d}t} = |\varepsilon| I = L I \frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\). Integrating from \(0\) to \(I\) gives the total magnetic energy stored in the inductor: \(U = \int_0^I L I \,\mathrm{d}I = \frac{1}{2}L I^2\).
4. The self-induced electromotive force opposes the change in current according to Faraday's and Lenz's laws, expressed as \(\varepsilon = -L\,\frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working and Evaluation
Matching each item to its governing formula:
- Self-inductance of a long solenoid corresponds to \(L = \mu_0 n^2 A l\).
- Mutual inductance of two coaxial solenoids corresponds to \(M = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 \pi r_1^2 l\).
- Magnetic potential energy stored in an inductor corresponds to \(U = \frac{1}{2}L I^2\).
- Back electromotive force induced in an inductor corresponds to \(\varepsilon = -L\,\frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The units and dimensions are consistent across all formulations: inductances scale with \(\mu_0 \times (\text{turns}/\text{length})^2 \times \text{volume}\), energy scales as \(L I^2\), and emf equals \(L \times \text{rate of change of current}\). The correct matching pairs self-inductance with \(\mu_0 n^2 A l\), mutual inductance with \(\mu_0 n_1 n_2 \pi r_1^2 l\), stored energy with \(\frac{1}{2} L I^2\), and back emf with \(-L\,\frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_CLASS12_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_MATCHING_Q04 - AC generator coil orientation and instantaneous values of flux and emf

questiontext.text:
An AC generator has a planar armature coil of \(N\) turns and area \(A\) rotating with constant angular speed \(\omega\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\mathbf{B}\). The angle \(\theta = \omega t\) is measured between the normal to the coil area vector \(\mathbf{A}\) and the magnetic field vector \(\mathbf{B}\). Match the orientation or state of the coil in List I with the corresponding instantaneous value of magnetic flux \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}\) or induced electromotive force \(\varepsilon\) in List II:

List I (Coil State / Orientation) List II (Flux / Induced EMF Value)
(A) Plane of coil perpendicular to \(\mathbf{B}\) (\(\theta = 0^{\circ}\)) (I) \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = 0\) and induced emf has maximum magnitude \(\varepsilon = \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega\)
(B) Plane of coil parallel to \(\mathbf{B}\) (\(\theta = 90^{\circ}\)) (II) \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = -N B A\) and induced emf is zero (\(\varepsilon = 0\))
(C) Armature rotated by half a revolution from initial position (\(\theta = 180^{\circ}\)) (III) Magnitude of the rate of change of magnetic flux \(\left|\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}t}\right|\) is zero
(D) Instant when magnetic flux through each turn is an extremum (\(\theta = 0^{\circ}\) or \(180^{\circ}\)) (IV) \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = +N B A\) and induced emf is zero (\(\varepsilon = 0\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
An AC generator coil of \(N\) turns and area \(A\) rotates with angular speed \(\omega\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\mathbf{B}\). The angle between the magnetic field vector and the normal to the coil is \(\theta = \omega t\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae and Principles
1. The total magnetic flux linked with the \(N\)-turn coil is given by: \[ \Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = N (\mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{A}) = N B A \cos(\omega t) = N B A \cos\theta \] 2. According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the instantaneous induced electromotive force is: \[ \varepsilon = -\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}t} = -\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}[N B A \cos(\omega t)] = N B A \omega \sin(\omega t) = \varepsilon_0 \sin\theta \] where \(\varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega\) is the peak electromotive force.

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working and Evaluation
Evaluating each orientation:
- When the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the area vector is aligned with \(\mathbf{B}\), giving \(\theta = 0^{\circ}\). Here, \(\cos(0^{\circ}) = 1\) so the magnetic flux is positive maximum, \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = +N B A\). The induced emf is \(\varepsilon = \varepsilon_0 \sin(0^{\circ}) = 0\).
- When the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field, the area vector is perpendicular to \(\mathbf{B}\), giving \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\). Here, \(\cos(90^{\circ}) = 0\) so the magnetic flux through the coil is zero, \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = 0\). Since \(\sin(90^{\circ}) = 1\), the induced emf attains its peak magnitude, \(\varepsilon = \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega\).
- When the coil is rotated by half a turn from the initial position, \(\theta = 180^{\circ}\). Here, \(\cos(180^{\circ}) = -1\) so the magnetic flux is negative maximum, \(\Phi_{\mathrm{B}} = -N B A\). The induced emf is \(\varepsilon = \varepsilon_0 \sin(180^{\circ}) = 0\).
- At the instants when the magnetic flux is an extremum (\(\theta = 0^{\circ}\) or \(180^{\circ}\)), the derivative of a cosine function at its extrema is zero. Hence, the magnitude of the rate of change of magnetic flux, \(\left|\frac{\mathrm{d}\Phi_{\mathrm{B}}}{\mathrm{d}t}\right| = N B A \omega |\sin\theta|\), is exactly zero, which corresponds to zero induced emf.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The sinusoidal relationship demonstrates a \(90^{\circ}\) phase shift between flux (proportional to cosine) and induced emf (proportional to sine). Maximum flux corresponds to zero emf, while zero flux corresponds to maximum rate of change of flux and maximum induced emf. The correct pairing matches the perpendicular plane with \(+N B A\) and zero emf, the parallel plane with zero flux and maximum emf, the half-revolution rotated coil with \(-N B A\) and zero emf, and the extremum flux state with zero rate of change of flux.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Magnetic flux through flat coil in perpendicular field

questiontext.text: A flat rectangular wire loop of area \( 0.050\text{ m}^2 \) is placed in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude \( 0.40\text{ T} \). If the normal to the plane of the loop is parallel to the direction of the magnetic field, what is the magnetic flux linked with the loop?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Surface area of loop: \( A = 0.050\text{ m}^2 \).
Magnetic field magnitude: \( B = 0.40\text{ T} \).
The area vector \( \mathbf{A} \) is parallel to \( \mathbf{B} \), so the angle is \( \theta = 0^\circ \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The magnetic field is spatially uniform and time-independent across the entire plane of the loop.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Magnetic flux through a planar surface is given by:
\[ \Phi_B = \mathbf{B} \cdot \mathbf{A} = B A \cos\theta \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numerical values:
\[ \Phi_B = (0.40\text{ T}) \times (0.050\text{ m}^2) \times \cos 0^\circ = 0.020 \times 1 = 0.020\text{ Wb} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{T}\cdot\text{m}^2 = \text{Wb} \). The magnetic flux linked with the loop is \( 0.020\text{ Wb} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Motional electromotive force across moving straight conductor

questiontext.text: A straight conducting rod of length \( 0.40\text{ m} \) moves at a constant speed of \( 5.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \) perpendicular to its own length and perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.50\text{ T} \). What is the motional electromotive force induced across the ends of the rod?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of conductor: \( l = 0.40\text{ m} \).
Speed of conductor: \( v = 5.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.50\text{ T} \).
The length vector, velocity vector, and magnetic field vector are mutually perpendicular.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The magnetic field is uniform and static across the region of motion.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The motional electromotive force induced in a straight conductor is given by:
\[ \varepsilon = B l v \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values into the formula:
\[ \varepsilon = (0.50\text{ T}) \times (0.40\text{ m}) \times (5.0\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 0.20 \times 5.0 = 1.0\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: \( [\text{T}][\text{m}][\text{m s}^{-1}] = [\text{V}] \). The induced electromotive force is \( 1.0\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Induced electromotive force in closely wound coil

questiontext.text: A closely wound coil of \( 100 \) turns is linked with a magnetic flux that changes by \( 0.050\text{ Wb} \) in a time interval of \( 0.20\text{ s} \). What is the magnitude of the average induced electromotive force in the coil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of turns: \( N = 100 \).
Change in magnetic flux per turn: \( |\Delta\Phi_B| = 0.050\text{ Wb} \).
Time interval: \( \Delta t = 0.20\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All turns are identical and experience the exact same flux variation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By Faraday's law of induction, the magnitude of the induced emf is:
\[ \varepsilon = N \frac{|\Delta\Phi_B|}{\Delta t} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numbers:
\[ \varepsilon = 100 \times \frac{0.050\text{ Wb}}{0.20\text{ s}} = 100 \times 0.25 = 25\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{Wb/s} = \text{V} \). The magnitude of the induced electromotive force is \( 25\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Back electromotive force in an active inductor

questiontext.text: An electric current in an inductor of self-inductance \( 2.0\text{ H} \) increases at a constant rate of \( 15\text{ A s}^{-1} \). What is the magnitude of the self-induced back electromotive force developed in the inductor?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Self-inductance: \( L = 2.0\text{ H} \).
Rate of change of current: \( \frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t} = 15\text{ A s}^{-1} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Resistive voltage drop across the inductor windings is neglected.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The self-induced back electromotive force is given by:
\[ |\varepsilon| = L \left|\frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t}\right| \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[ |\varepsilon| = (2.0\text{ H}) \times (15\text{ A s}^{-1}) = 30\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{H}\cdot\text{A/s} = (\text{V}\cdot\text{s/A})\cdot(\text{A/s}) = \text{V} \). The magnitude of the back emf is \( 30\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Magnetic potential energy stored in pure inductor

questiontext.text: What is the magnetic potential energy stored in an inductor of self-inductance \( 0.40\text{ H} \) when carrying a steady electric current of \( 5.0\text{ A} \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Self-inductance: \( L = 0.40\text{ H} \).
Current: \( I = 5.0\text{ A} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The inductor operates in its linear magnetic regime below core saturation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic potential energy stored in an inductor is given by:
\[ U_B = \frac{1}{2} L I^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( I^2 \): \( (5.0\text{ A})^2 = 25\text{ A}^2 \).
Substitute into the formula:
\[ U_B = \frac{1}{2} \times (0.40\text{ H}) \times (25\text{ A}^2) = 0.20 \times 25 = 5.0\text{ J} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{H}\cdot\text{A}^2 = (\text{J/A}^2)\cdot\text{A}^2 = \text{J} \). The stored magnetic potential energy is \( 5.0\text{ J} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Peak voltage calculation for rotating armature coil

questiontext.text: An AC generator armature coil consists of \( 50 \) turns, each having an area of \( 0.040\text{ m}^2 \). The coil is rotated at a constant angular speed of \( 100\text{ rad s}^{-1} \) in a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.20\text{ T} \) perpendicular to the axis of rotation. What is the peak (maximum) electromotive force generated?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of turns: \( N = 50 \).
Area of coil: \( A = 0.040\text{ m}^2 \).
Angular velocity: \( \omega = 100\text{ rad s}^{-1} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.20\text{ T} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The rotation axis is perpendicular to the uniform magnetic field.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The peak electromotive force generated in an AC alternator is:
\[ \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[ \varepsilon_0 = 50 \times (0.20\text{ T}) \times (0.040\text{ m}^2) \times (100\text{ rad s}^{-1}) \]
\[ \varepsilon_0 = 10 \times 4.0 = 40\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking calculation: \( 50 \times 0.2 \times 0.04 \times 100 = 40\text{ V} \). The peak electromotive force is \( 40\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Magnetic flux linkage from mutual inductance change

questiontext.text: A pair of mutually coupled coils has a mutual inductance of \( 0.80\text{ H} \\). If the electric current in the primary coil increases by \( 10\text{ A} \), what is the magnitude of the change in magnetic flux linkage in the secondary coil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mutual inductance: \( M = 0.80\text{ H} \).
Change in primary current: \( \Delta I_1 = 10\text{ A} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The relative orientation and position of the coils remain fixed.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The change in magnetic flux linkage in the secondary coil is given by:
\[ \Delta(N_2 \Phi_2) = M \,\Delta I_1 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numbers:
\[ \Delta(N_2 \Phi_2) = (0.80\text{ H}) \times (10\text{ A}) = 8.0\text{ Wb} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{H}\cdot\text{A} = (\text{Wb/A})\cdot\text{A} = \text{Wb} \). The change in flux linkage is \( 8.0\text{ Wb} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Flux calculation across tilted square wire coil

questiontext.text: A flat square coil of side \( 10\text{ cm} \) is placed in a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.80\text{ T} \). If the plane of the coil makes an angle of \( 30^\circ \) with the magnetic field lines, what is the magnetic flux linked with the coil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Side of square: \( s = 10\text{ cm} = 0.10\text{ m} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.80\text{ T} \).
Angle between plane of coil and field lines: \( \alpha = 30^\circ \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The area vector \( \mathbf{A} \) is perpendicular to the plane of the coil. Therefore, the angle between \( \mathbf{A} \) and \( \mathbf{B} \) is \( \theta = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Area of coil: \( A = s^2 \).
Magnetic flux: \( \Phi_B = B A \cos\theta \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate area: \( A = (0.10\text{ m})^2 = 0.010\text{ m}^2 \).
Calculate flux:
\[ \Phi_B = (0.80\text{ T}) \times (0.010\text{ m}^2) \times \cos 60^\circ = 0.0080 \times 0.50 = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ Wb} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking values: \( 0.80 \times 0.01 \times 0.5 = 0.0040\text{ Wb} \). The magnetic flux linked with the coil is \( 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ Wb} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Induced emf and current in square loop

questiontext.text: A square loop of side \( 10\text{ cm} \) and resistance \( 0.50\ \Omega \) is held vertically in the east-west plane. A uniform magnetic field of \( 0.10\text{ T} \) is set up across the plane in the north-east direction. The magnetic field is decreased steadily to zero in \( 0.70\text{ s} \). What are the magnitudes of the induced electromotive force and electric current? (Take \( \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Side: \( s = 0.10\text{ m} \), Resistance: \( R = 0.50\ \Omega \).
Initial field: \( B = 0.10\text{ T} \), Final field: \( 0\text{ T} \).
Time interval: \( \Delta t = 0.70\text{ s} \).
The area vector points north, making angle \( \theta = 45^\circ \) with north-east field.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Field decreases linearly with time, ensuring a constant induced emf.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Initial flux: \( \Phi = B s^2 \cos 45^\circ = \frac{0.10 \times 10^{-2}}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ Wb} = \frac{10^{-3}}{\sqrt{2}}\text{ Wb} \).
Induced emf: \( \varepsilon = \frac{\Phi}{\Delta t} \).
Induced current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ \varepsilon = \frac{10^{-3}}{\sqrt{2} \times 0.70} = \frac{10^{-3}}{1.414 \times 0.70} \approx 1.01 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} = 1.0\text{ mV} \]
\[ I = \frac{1.01 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V}}{0.50\ \Omega} \approx 2.02 \times 10^{-3}\text{ A} = 2.0\text{ mA} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The induced electromotive force is \( 1.0\text{ mV} \) and the induced electric current is \( 2.0\text{ mA} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Induced electromotive force in rotated multiturn coil

questiontext.text: A circular coil of radius \( 10\text{ cm} \) having \( 500 \) turns is oriented with its plane perpendicular to the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field (\( B_H = 3.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T} \)). It is flipped through \( 180^\circ \) about its vertical diameter in \( 0.25\text{ s} \). What is the estimated magnitude of the average induced electromotive force? (Take \( \pi \approx 3.1416 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius: \( r = 0.10\text{ m} \), Turns: \( N = 500 \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 3.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T} \).
Flip angle: \( 180^\circ \), Duration: \( \Delta t = 0.25\text{ s} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Initial angle \( \theta_1 = 0^\circ \), final angle \( \theta_2 = 180^\circ \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Area: \( A = \pi r^2 = \pi (0.10)^2 = 0.01\pi\text{ m}^2 \).
Change in flux per turn: \( \Delta\Phi = B A [\cos 180^\circ - \cos 0^\circ] = -2 B A \).
Average induced emf magnitude: \( \varepsilon = N \frac{2 B A}{\Delta t} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ 2 B A = 2 \times (3.0 \times 10^{-5}) \times (0.01\pi) = 6.0\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ Wb} \]
\[ \varepsilon = 500 \times \frac{6.0\pi \times 10^{-7}}{0.25} = 2000 \times 6.0\pi \times 10^{-7} = 1.2\pi \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} \approx 3.77 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} \approx 3.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking calculation: \( 1.2 \times 3.1416 \times 10^{-3} = 3.77 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} \approx 3.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} \). The average induced emf is \( 3.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Current calculation in circular loop under changing field

questiontext.text: A circular conducting loop of radius \( 7.0\text{ cm} \) and total electrical resistance \( 0.40\ \Omega \) is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. If the magnetic field increases at a steady rate of \( 2.0\text{ T s}^{-1} \), what is the magnitude of the induced electric current in the loop? (Take \( \pi \approx \frac{22}{7} \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Radius of loop: \( r = 7.0\text{ cm} = 0.070\text{ m} \).
Resistance: \( R = 0.40\ \Omega \).
Rate of change of magnetic field: \( \frac{\mathrm{d}B}{\mathrm{d}t} = 2.0\text{ T s}^{-1} \).
Field is normal to loop plane, so \( \theta = 0^\circ \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Self-inductance of the single loop is negligible.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Area: \( A = \pi r^2 \).
Induced emf: \( \varepsilon = A \frac{\mathrm{d}B}{\mathrm{d}t} \).
Induced current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate area: \( A = \frac{22}{7} \times (0.070\text{ m})^2 = \frac{22}{7} \times 0.0049\text{ m}^2 = 0.0154\text{ m}^2 \).
Calculate induced emf:
\[ \varepsilon = (0.0154\text{ m}^2) \times (2.0\text{ T s}^{-1}) = 0.0308\text{ V} \]
Calculate induced current:
\[ I = \frac{0.0308\text{ V}}{0.40\ \Omega} = 0.077\text{ A} = 77\text{ mA} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{V}/\\Omega = \text{A} \). The induced electric current is \( 77\text{ mA} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Total induced charge through cross section of circuit

questiontext.text: A closed coil of total electrical resistance \( 10\ \Omega \) is placed in a magnetic field. The magnetic flux linked with the coil decreases steadily from \( 12\text{ Wb} \) to \( 4.0\text{ Wb} \). What is the total electric charge that passes through any cross-section of the coil during this flux change?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance of coil: \( R = 10\ \Omega \).
Initial magnetic flux: \( \Phi_1 = 12\text{ Wb} \).
Final magnetic flux: \( \Phi_2 = 4.0\text{ Wb} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Self-inductance of the coil is assumed negligible.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The total charge flown during a flux change \( \Delta\Phi \) is given by:
\[ \Delta Q = \frac{|\Delta\Phi|}{R} = \frac{|\Phi_2 - \Phi_1|}{R} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Change in flux: \( |\Delta\Phi| = |4.0\text{ Wb} - 12\text{ Wb}| = 8.0\text{ Wb} \).
Calculate charge flown:
\[ \Delta Q = \frac{8.0\text{ Wb}}{10\ \Omega} = 0.80\text{ C} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: \( \text{Wb}/\\Omega = (\text{V}\cdot\text{s})/(\text{V/A}) = \text{A}\cdot\text{s} = \text{C} \). The total charge is \( 0.80\text{ C} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Electromotive force across revolving metallic circular contact

questiontext.text: A \( 1.0\text{ m} \) long metallic rod is rotated with an angular frequency of \( 400\text{ rad s}^{-1} \) about an axis normal to the rod passing through one of its ends. The other end of the rod makes continuous sliding contact with a circular metallic ring. A constant and uniform magnetic field of \( 0.50\text{ T} \) parallel to the axis exists everywhere. What is the electromotive force developed between the centre and the ring?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of rod: \( R = 1.0\text{ m} \).
Angular velocity: \( \omega = 400\text{ rad s}^{-1} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.50\text{ T} \) parallel to the rotation axis.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The plane of rotation is perpendicular to the uniform magnetic field.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The electromotive force induced across a rod rotating about one end is:
\[ \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[ \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times (0.50\text{ T}) \times (400\text{ rad s}^{-1}) \times (1.0\text{ m})^2 = 0.25 \times 400 = 100\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking dimensions: \( [\text{T}][\text{s}^{-1}][\text{m}^2] = [\text{V}] \). The electromotive force developed is \( 100\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Electromotive force across rotating bicycle wheel spokes

questiontext.text: A wheel with \( 10 \) metallic spokes, each of length \( 0.50\text{ m} \), is rotated with a speed of \( 120\text{ rev/min} \) in a plane normal to the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field (\( B_H = 0.40\text{ G} = 0.40 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T} \)). What is the induced electromotive force between the central axle and the rim of the wheel? (Take \( \pi \approx 3.1416 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of spokes: \( 10 \).
Length of spoke: \( R = 0.50\text{ m} \).
Rotational frequency: \( \nu = \frac{120}{60}\text{ rev/s} = 2.0\text{ rev/s} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.40 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
All \( 10 \) spokes are identical and connected in parallel between the axle and the conducting rim. The total emf equals that of a single spoke.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Angular speed: \( \omega = 2\pi \nu = 4\pi\text{ rad s}^{-1} \).
Induced emf: \( \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega R^2 \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[ \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times (0.40 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T}) \times (4\pi\text{ rad s}^{-1}) \times (0.50\text{ m})^2 \]
\[ \varepsilon = (0.20 \times 10^{-4}) \times (4\pi) \times 0.25 = 0.20\pi \times 10^{-4}\text{ V} \approx 6.28 \times 10^{-5}\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Evaluating: \( 0.20 \times 3.1416 \times 10^{-4} = 6.2832 \times 10^{-5}\text{ V} \). The induced electromotive force is \( 6.28 \times 10^{-5}\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Instantaneous voltage in falling horizontal east west wire

questiontext.text: A horizontal straight wire of length \( 10\text{ m} \) oriented east to west falls freely under gravity with a speed of \( 5.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \) at right angles to the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field, \( 0.30 \times 10^{-4}\text{ Wb m}^{-2} \). What is the instantaneous value of the electromotive force induced in the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of wire: \( l = 10\text{ m} \).
Speed of fall: \( v = 5.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \).
Horizontal component of magnetic field: \( B = 0.30 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T} \).
Velocity, wire orientation, and field are mutually perpendicular.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The Earth's magnetic field is locally uniform.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Motional emf in a straight conductor:
\[ \varepsilon = B l v \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[ \varepsilon = (0.30 \times 10^{-4}\text{ T}) \times (10\text{ m}) \times (5.0\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} = 1.5\text{ mV} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking calculation: \( 0.30 \times 10^{-4} \times 50 = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ V} = 1.5\text{ mV} \). The instantaneous induced emf is \( 1.5\text{ mV} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Inductance calculation from collapsing electric circuit current

questiontext.text: Electric current in a circuit falls steadily from \( 5.0\text{ A} \) to \( 0.0\text{ A} \) in \( 0.10\text{ s} \). If an average electromotive force of \( 200\text{ V} \) is induced, what is the estimated self-inductance of the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial current: \( I_1 = 5.0\text{ A} \), Final current: \( I_2 = 0.0\text{ A} \).
Time interval: \( \Delta t = 0.10\text{ s} \).
Average induced emf: \( |\varepsilon| = 200\text{ V} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The decay of current is linear with time.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The self-induced emf is related to self-inductance by:
\[ |\varepsilon| = L \frac{|\Delta I|}{\Delta t} \implies L = \frac{|\varepsilon| \Delta t}{|\Delta I|} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Change in current: \( |\Delta I| = |0.0 - 5.0| = 5.0\text{ A} \).
Substitute into the expression:
\[ L = \frac{(200\text{ V}) \times (0.10\text{ s})}{5.0\text{ A}} = \frac{20\text{ V}\cdot\text{s}}{5.0\text{ A}} = 4.0\text{ H} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{V}\cdot\text{s/A} = \text{H} \). The estimated self-inductance is \( 4.0\text{ H} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Self inductance of cylindrical air core solenoid

questiontext.text: A long air-core solenoid of length \( 0.50\text{ m} \) and cross-sectional radius \( 2.0\text{ cm} \) has a total of \( 500 \) closely wound turns. What is the self-inductance of this solenoid? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A} \) and \( \pi^2 \approx 9.87 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of solenoid: \( l = 0.50\text{ m} \).
Radius: \( r = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.020\text{ m} \).
Total turns: \( N = 500 \).
Permeability of free space: \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The solenoid is sufficiently long that end fringing effects of the magnetic field can be neglected.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Cross-sectional area: \( A = \pi r^2 \).
Self-inductance of a long solenoid in terms of total turns:
\[ L = \frac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Area: \( A = \pi (0.020\text{ m})^2 = 4.0\pi \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2 \).
Turns squared: \( N^2 = (500)^2 = 2.5 \times 10^5 \).
Calculate self-inductance:
\[ L = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times (2.5 \times 10^5) \times (4.0\pi \times 10^{-4})}{0.50} \]
\[ L = \frac{40\pi^2 \times 10^{-6}}{0.50} = 80\pi^2 \times 10^{-6}\text{ H} \]
With \( \pi^2 \approx 9.87 \):
\[ L \approx 80 \times 9.87 \times 10^{-6}\text{ H} = 789.6 \times 10^{-6}\text{ H} \approx 0.79\text{ mH} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Evaluating: \( 7.9 \times 10^{-4}\text{ H} = 0.79\text{ mH} \). The self-inductance is \( 0.79\text{ mH} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Energy density of strong uniform magnetic field

questiontext.text: A high-field laboratory electromagnet produces a uniform magnetic field of \( 2.0\text{ T} \) in air. What is the magnetic energy stored per unit volume in this field? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\\cdot\text{m/A} \) and \( \pi \approx 3.1416 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Magnetic field: \( B = 2.0\text{ T} \).
Permeability of free space: \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The medium is non-magnetic air (relative permeability \( \mu_r \approx 1 \)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnetic energy density (energy per unit volume) is given by:
\[ u_B = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( B^2 \): \( (2.0\text{ T})^2 = 4.0\text{ T}^2 \).
Substitute into the formula:
\[ u_B = \frac{4.0}{2 \times (4\pi \times 10^{-7})} = \frac{4.0}{8\pi \times 10^{-7}} = \frac{10^7}{2\pi} = \frac{10^7}{6.2832} \approx 1.59 \times 10^6\text{ J m}^{-3} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking magnitude: \( 10^7 / 6.2832 \approx 1.59 \times 10^6\text{ J m}^{-3} \). The magnetic energy density is \( 1.59 \times 10^6\text{ J m}^{-3} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q19 - Mutual inductance between coaxial cylindrical solenoids

questiontext.text: Two long coaxial solenoids of the same length \( 1.0\text{ m} \) are wound one over the other. The inner solenoid has radius \( r_1 = 2.0\text{ cm} \) and \( n_1 = 1000\text{ turns/m} \), while the outer solenoid has \( n_2 = 2000\text{ turns/m} \). What is the mutual inductance of this coaxial solenoid pair? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A} \) and \( \pi^2 \approx 9.87 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of solenoids: \( l = 1.0\text{ m} \).
Inner radius: \( r_1 = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.020\text{ m} \).
Turn densities: \( n_1 = 1000\text{ m}^{-1} \), \( n_2 = 2000\text{ m}^{-1} \).
Medium inside solenoids is air.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The solenoids are long compared to the outer radius, so end fringing effects can be neglected.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Mutual inductance of two long coaxial solenoids is given by:
\[ M = \mu_0 n_1 n_2 (\pi r_1^2) l \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Area of inner solenoid: \( \pi r_1^2 = \pi (0.020\text{ m})^2 = 4.0\pi \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2 \).
Calculate product \( n_1 n_2 = 1000 \times 2000 = 2.0 \times 10^6\text{ m}^{-2} \).
Substitute into formula:
\[ M = (4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times (2.0 \times 10^6) \times (4.0\pi \times 10^{-4}) \times 1.0 \]
\[ M = 32\pi^2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ H} = 3.2\pi^2 \times 10^{-4}\text{ H} \]
With \( \pi^2 \approx 9.87 \):
\[ M \approx 3.2 \times 9.87 \times 10^{-4}\text{ H} \approx 31.58 \times 10^{-4}\text{ H} \approx 3.16\text{ mH} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Evaluating: \( 3.16 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H} = 3.16\text{ mH} \). The mutual inductance is \( 3.16\text{ mH} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q20 - Mutual inductance between concentric circular wire loops

questiontext.text: Two flat circular coils of single turn are placed coplanar with concentric centres. The inner coil has radius \( r_1 = 1.0\text{ cm} \) and the outer coil has radius \( r_2 = 20\text{ cm} \) (satisfying \( r_1 \ll r_2 \)). What is the mutual inductance of this arrangement? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A} \) and \( \pi^2 \approx 9.87 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Inner coil radius: \( r_1 = 1.0\text{ cm} = 0.010\text{ m} \).
Outer coil radius: \( r_2 = 20\text{ cm} = 0.20\text{ m} \).
Coils are coplanar and concentric, with \( r_1 \ll r_2 \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Because \( r_1 \ll r_2 \), the magnetic field produced by the outer coil at its centre is treated as uniform across the area of the inner coil.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Mutual inductance of concentric circular coils is given by:
\[ M = \frac{\mu_0 \pi r_1^2}{2 r_2} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( r_1^2 = (0.010\text{ m})^2 = 1.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2 \).
Denominator: \( 2 r_2 = 2 \times 0.20\text{ m} = 0.40\text{ m} \).
Substitute into formula:
\[ M = \frac{(4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times \pi \times (1.0 \times 10^{-4})}{0.40} = \frac{4\pi^2 \times 10^{-11}}{0.40} = 10\pi^2 \times 10^{-11}\text{ H} \]
\[ M = \pi^2 \times 10^{-10}\text{ H} \approx 9.87 \times 10^{-10}\text{ H} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Evaluating: \( 9.87 \times 10^{-10}\text{ H} \approx 0.99\text{ nH} \). The mutual inductance is \( 9.87 \times 10^{-10}\text{ H} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q21 - Electromotive force induced by primary current variation

questiontext.text: A pair of mutually coupled coils has a mutual inductance of \( 0.25\text{ H} \). If the electric current in the primary coil changes at a constant rate of \( 40\text{ A s}^{-1} \), what is the magnitude of the electromotive force induced across the terminals of the secondary coil?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mutual inductance: \( M = 0.25\text{ H} \).
Rate of change of primary current: \( \frac{\mathrm{d}I_1}{\mathrm{d}t} = 40\text{ A s}^{-1} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Coils are stationary relative to each other.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The magnitude of the mutually induced electromotive force is:
\[ |\varepsilon_2| = M \left|\frac{\mathrm{d}I_1}{\mathrm{d}t}\right| \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values:
\[ |\varepsilon_2| = (0.25\text{ H}) \times (40\text{ A s}^{-1}) = 10\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{H}\cdot\text{A/s} = \text{V} \). The magnitude of the induced emf is \( 10\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q22 - Maximum voltage generated by pedal alternator coil

questiontext.text: A stationary bicycle pedal drives a flat generator coil of \( 100 \) turns, each of cross-sectional area \( 0.10\text{ m}^2 \). The coil rotates at a constant rate of \( 0.50\text{ rev/s} \) in a uniform magnetic field of \( 0.010\text{ T} \) directed perpendicular to the rotation axis. What is the maximum voltage generated in the coil? (Take \( \pi \approx 3.1416 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of turns: \( N = 100 \).
Area: \( A = 0.10 ext{ m}^2 \).
Frequency: \( u = 0.50 ext{ Hz} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.010 ext{ T} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Uniform rotation with angular velocity \( \omega = 2\pi u \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The maximum generated voltage is given by:
\[ \varepsilon_0 = N B A \omega = N B A (2\pi u) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute into the formula:
\[ \varepsilon_0 = 100 imes (0.010 ext{ T}) imes (0.10 ext{ m}^2) imes (2 imes 3.1416 imes 0.50 ext{ s}^{-1}) \]
\[ \varepsilon_0 = (1.0) imes (0.10) imes (3.1416) = 0.31416 ext{ V} \approx 0.314 ext{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Evaluating: \( 0.10 imes 3.1416 = 0.314 ext{ V} \). The maximum voltage generated is \( 0.314 ext{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q23 - Instantaneous voltage produced by alternating current generator

questiontext.text: An AC generator generates an alternating electromotive force with a peak amplitude of \( 200\text{ V} \) at a commercial frequency of \( 50\text{ Hz} \). Assuming the electromotive force is zero at time \( t = 0 \), what is the instantaneous electromotive force at time \( t = \frac{1}{600}\text{ s} \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Peak voltage: \( \varepsilon_0 = 200 ext{ V} \).
Frequency: \( u = 50 ext{ Hz} \).
Time instant: \( t = rac{1}{600} ext{ s} \).
Initial condition: \( \varepsilon(0) = 0 \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The generated emf varies sinusoidally as \( \varepsilon(t) = \varepsilon_0 \sin(2\pi u t) \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Instantaneous emf:
\[ \varepsilon(t) = \varepsilon_0 \sin(\omega t) = \varepsilon_0 \sin(2\pi u t) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate phase angle:
\[ heta = 2\pi imes 50 imes rac{1}{600} = rac{100\pi}{600} = rac{\pi}{6} ext{ rad} = 30^\circ \]
Evaluate sine:
\[ \sin\left( rac{\pi}{6} ight) = rac{1}{2} = 0.50 \]
Calculate instantaneous voltage:
\[ \varepsilon = 200 ext{ V} imes 0.50 = 100 ext{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
At one-twelfth of the period, \( \sin(\pi/6) = 0.5 \), so \( \varepsilon = 100 ext{ V} \). The instantaneous electromotive force is \( 100 ext{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q24 - Induced electric current in rail conductor circuit

questiontext.text: A straight conducting rod of length \( 0.50\text{ m} \) and negligible internal resistance moves at a constant speed of \( 4.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \) along two parallel conducting rails. The rails are connected across an external resistor of resistance \( 2.0\ \Omega \). A uniform magnetic field of \( 0.80\text{ T} \) is directed perpendicular to the plane of the rails. What is the magnitude of the induced electric current flowing through the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Rod length: \( l = 0.50\text{ m} \).
Speed: \( v = 4.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \).
Resistance: \( R = 2.0\ \Omega \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.80\text{ T} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Frictional forces and rail resistance are negligible.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Motional induced emf: \( \varepsilon = B l v \).
Induced current by Ohm's law: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R} = \frac{B l v}{R} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate induced emf:
\[ \varepsilon = (0.80\text{ T}) \times (0.50\text{ m}) \times (4.0\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 1.6\text{ V} \]
Calculate induced current:
\[ I = \frac{1.6\text{ V}}{2.0\ \Omega} = 0.80\text{ A} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \( \text{V}/\\Omega = \text{A} \). The magnitude of the induced electric current is \( 0.80\text{ A} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q25 - Inductance enhancement by ferromagnetic soft iron core

questiontext.text: An air-core long solenoid has a self-inductance of \( 1.5\text{ mH} \). If the interior of the solenoid is completely filled with a soft iron core having a relative magnetic permeability of \( \mu_r = 600 \), what is the new self-inductance of the solenoid?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial self-inductance: \( L_0 = 1.5\text{ mH} = 1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H} \).
Relative magnetic permeability: \( \mu_r = 600 \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Core material fills the entire flux-carrying cross section uniformly.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The self-inductance with a magnetic core of relative permeability \( \mu_r \) is:
\[ L = \mu_r L_0 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute into the expression:
\[ L = 600 \times (1.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H}) = 900 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H} = 0.90\text{ H} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Multiplying: \( 600 \times 1.5\text{ mH} = 900\text{ mH} = 0.90\text{ H} \). The new self-inductance is \( 0.90\text{ H} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q26 - Electromotive force in loop inside powered solenoid

questiontext.text: A long solenoid with \( 15\text{ turns per cm} \) has a small circular wire loop of area \( 2.0\text{ cm}^2 \) placed inside near its centre with its plane perpendicular to the solenoid's axis. If the current carried by the solenoid increases steadily from \( 2.0\text{ A} \) to \( 4.0\text{ A} \) in \( 0.10\text{ s} \), what is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force in the loop? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A} \) and \( \pi \approx 3.142 \))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Turn density: \( n = 15\text{ cm}^{-1} = 1500\text{ m}^{-1} \).
Loop area: \( A = 2.0\text{ cm}^2 = 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2 \).
Current change: \( \Delta I = 4.0\text{ A} - 2.0\text{ A} = 2.0\text{ A} \).
Time interval: \( \Delta t = 0.10\text{ s} \).
Plane of loop is normal to axis, so \( \theta = 0^\circ \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The solenoid is long, so the magnetic field inside is uniform: \( B = \mu_0 n I \).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Rate of change of magnetic field: \( \frac{\mathrm{d}B}{\mathrm{d}t} = \mu_0 n \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \).
Induced emf in the loop: \( \varepsilon = A \frac{\mathrm{d}B}{\mathrm{d}t} = A \mu_0 n \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \( \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} = \frac{2.0\text{ A}}{0.10\text{ s}} = 20\text{ A s}^{-1} \).
Substitute into formula:
\[ \varepsilon = (2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2) \times (4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}\cdot\text{m/A}) \times (1500\text{ m}^{-1}) \times (20\text{ A s}^{-1}) \]
\[ \varepsilon = (2.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times (4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times 30000 \]
\[ \varepsilon = 24\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ V} \approx 24 \times 3.1416 \times 10^{-7}\text{ V} \approx 7.54 \times 10^{-6}\text{ V} \approx 7.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ V} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Evaluating: \( 24\pi \times 10^{-7} \approx 7.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ V} \). The magnitude of the induced electromotive force is \( 7.5 \times 10^{-6}\text{ V} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q27 - Induced electromotive force exiting along longer edge

questiontext.text: A rectangular wire loop of sides \( 8.0\text{ cm} \) and \( 2.0\text{ cm} \) with a small cut is pulled out of a region of uniform magnetic field \( B = 0.30\text{ T} \) (normal to the loop) at a constant velocity of \( 1.0\text{ cm s}^{-1} \). When the loop is moved normal to its longer side (length \( 8.0\text{ cm} \)), what is the induced electromotive force across the cut and for how long does this voltage persist?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Longer side: \( a = 8.0\text{ cm} = 0.080\text{ m} \).
Shorter side: \( b = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.020\text{ m} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 0.30\text{ T} \).
Speed: \( v = 1.0\text{ cm s}^{-1} = 0.010\text{ m s}^{-1} \).
The motion is normal to the longer side, meaning the active cutting edge has length \( l = a = 8.0\text{ cm} = 0.080\text{ m} \), and the distance traversed to exit the field is the shorter side \( b = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.020\text{ m} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The magnetic field is spatially uniform inside the boundary and zero outside.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Induced motional emf: \( \varepsilon = B l v \).
Duration of induced voltage: \( \Delta t = \frac{b}{v} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate induced emf:
\[ \varepsilon = (0.30\text{ T}) \times (0.080\text{ m}) \times (0.010\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 2.4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V} \]
Calculate duration:
\[ \Delta t = \frac{2.0\text{ cm}}{1.0\text{ cm s}^{-1}} = 2.0\text{ s} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Moving normal to the longer side produces an induced emf of \( 2.4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V} \) lasting for \( 2.0\text{ s} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q28 - Magnetic retarding force and electrical power dissipation

questiontext.text: A conducting rod of length \( 0.50\text{ m} \) and resistance \( 0.20\ \Omega \) slides with a constant velocity of \( 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \) on two frictionless horizontal rails. The rails are connected across an external resistor of \( 1.0\ \Omega \). A uniform magnetic field of \( 1.2\text{ T} \) is directed vertically downwards. What external mechanical force is required to sustain this motion, and what is the electrical power dissipated as heat in the circuit?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Length of rod: \( l = 0.50\text{ m} \).
Internal resistance of rod: \( r = 0.20\ \Omega \).
External resistor: \( R = 1.0\ \Omega \).
Total resistance: \( R_{\text{tot}} = R + r = 1.0 + 0.20 = 1.2\ \Omega \).
Speed: \( v = 6.0\text{ m s}^{-1} \).
Magnetic field: \( B = 1.2\text{ T} \).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Rails have negligible resistance, and mechanical friction is zero.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Motional emf: \( \varepsilon = B l v \).
Induced current: \( I = \frac{\varepsilon}{R_{\text{tot}}} = \frac{B l v}{R_{\text{tot}}} \).
Magnetic retarding force: \( F = I l B = \frac{B^2 l^2 v}{R_{\text{tot}}} \).
Power dissipated: \( P = F v = I^2 R_{\text{tot}} \).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate induced emf:
\[ \varepsilon = (1.2\text{ T}) \times (0.50\text{ m}) \times (6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 3.6\text{ V} \]
Calculate induced current:
\[ I = \frac{3.6\text{ V}}{1.2\ \Omega} = 3.0\text{ A} \]
Calculate external mechanical force:
\[ F = I l B = (3.0\text{ A}) \times (0.50\text{ m}) \times (1.2\text{ T}) = 1.8\text{ N} \]
Calculate power dissipated:
\[ P = F v = (1.8\text{ N}) \times (6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 10.8\text{ W} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verify using Joule heat: \( I^2 R_{\text{tot}} = (3.0)^2 \times 1.2 = 9.0 \times 1.2 = 10.8\text{ W} \). The required force is \( 1.8\text{ N} \) and the dissipated power is \( 10.8\text{ W} \).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_ELECTROMAGNETIC_INDUCTION_NUMERICAL_Q29 - Electromotive force induced in rotating quadrant frame
